15. Texas Rangers (71-73) 14. Cleveland Guardians (73-71) 13. Toronto Blue Jays (72-72) 12. Houston Astros (73-71) 11. Chicago White Sox (75-68)

With the Astros and Rangers both posting a 4-3 record last week, Houston maintained its two-game lead in the AL West standings. The two clubs are finished playing head-to-head, and the difference in remaining schedule difficulty is negligible, so the Rangers might need to get hot.

On the flip side, the Guardians trimmed a game off the White Sox advantage in the AL Central race, and the South Siders are now just 2.5 games up as they try to go worst-to-first in the division standings. The Guardians also hold a one-game lead for the No. 3 wild-card spot.

The Blue Jays were 52-60 heading into deadline day and opted to sell off some veteran pieces, but they are tied for the AL's best record since then at 20-12. With a .691 OPS that ranks 27th in the majors, they are an entirely different team than the one that reached the World Series a year ago on the strength of their high-powered offense.

Previous Rank: No. 11 Last Week: 1-2 @ CIN, 2-1 vs. NYY

The Padres have not won consecutive games since Aug. 23, and they suffered three straight series losses before taking two of three from the Yankees over the weekend. Michael King tossed six shutout innings in the series clincher on Sunday, and he now has a 2.26 ERA and seven quality starts in 10 games since the All-Star break.

Previous Rank: No. 10 Last Week: 1-2 vs. PHI, 2-1 @ HOU

Former NL Cy Young winner Corbin Burnes is expected to make his long-awaited return from Tommy John surgery on Tuesday against the Royals, giving the D-backs a huge September X-factor. As they continue to jockey for position with the Padres in the wild-card race, their season-ending matchup in San Diego is shaping up to potentially be huge.

Previous Rank: No. 8 Last Week: 1-2 vs. SEA, 4-0 @ BAL

The legend of Mickey Gasper added another chapter on Friday when his solo home run was the difference in a 1-0 victory over the Orioles. The veteran journeyman went 12-for-30 with six home runs in August, and he is one of a long list of players making a surprise impact for the Red Sox this year.

Previous Rank: No. 6 Last Week: 2-1 @ ARI, 1-2 vs. ATL

A six-game winning streak had the Phillies within three games of the Braves in the NL East race, but they lost three of four to close out last week, including two head-to-head with Atlanta. They have a five-game cushion in the wild-card standings, but also play the third-toughest remaining schedule, so there is still work to do.

Previous Rank: No. 5 Last Week: 2-1 @ LAA, 1-2 @ SD

The biggest story for the Yankees last week was undoubtedly Aaron Judge taking live batting practice with the team on Friday at Petco Park, as he took another step toward returning from a fractured rib that has sidelined him since May 31. Home series against the Rockies and Mets next week provide a golden opportunity to cut into Tampa Bay's four-game division lead.

Previous Rank: No. 7 Last Week: 2-2 vs. MIL, 2-1 @ MIA

Pete Crow-Armstrong hit his 40th home run of the season on Sunday, giving the Cubs their first 40-homer slugger since Derrek Lee in 2005. He is now seven steals away from joining the illustrious 40/40 club with 18 games remaining. Zooming out, the Cubs lead the majors in runs scored (768), home runs (201) and OPS (.771).

Previous Rank: No. 4 Last Week: 1-2 vs. NYM, 2-2 @ TEX

With 16 of their final 19 games against teams with a winning record, the Rays still need to get what would be the fifth division title in franchise history across the finish line. Deadline pickup Freddy Peralta has allowed five hits and one earned run in 12 innings over his last two starts, as he is building some nice momentum toward October.

Previous Rank: No. 3 Last Week: 1-2 vs. STL, 3-0 vs. WAS

Despite a bumpy 3-6 stretch prior to sweeping the Nationals over the weekend, the Dodgers still hold baseball's biggest division lead at 10.5 games. Mookie Betts is hitting .333/.404/.595 with five doubles, two home runs and 11 RBI in his last 10 games, and getting him producing at a high level after a modest season overall would be a boon to their already rosy October outlook.

Previous Rank: No. 2 Last Week: 0-1 vs. SF, 1-1 @ WAS, 2-1 @ PHI

The Braves have the best record in the NL since the All-Star break at 30-18, and a series victory over the Phillies at Citizens Bank Park helped pad their lead to five games in the NL East standings. It has been a down year overall for Ronald Acuña Jr., but he is getting hot at the perfect time after going 11-for-25 with three home runs last week.

Previous Rank: No. 1 Last Week: 2-2 @ CHC, 1-2 @ CIN

A 3-4 week on the road against a pair of division foes was not enough to keep the Brewers from occupying the No. 1 spot for the fifth straight week. With a 2.13 ERA, 0.69 WHIP and a 59-to-7 strikeout-to-walk ratio over 55 innings since the All-Star break, Logan Henderson has made a compelling case to be the No. 2 starter in October.

articles.title: Updated New York Yankees Playoff Predictions, Aaron Judge Projections for Final Stretch
articles.summary: With three weeks remaining in Major League Baseball's 2026 regular season, there is no longer any realistic scenario in which the New York Yankees fail to reach the postseason.
articles.body:
With three weeks remaining in Major League Baseball's 2026 regular season, there is no longer any realistic scenario in which the New York Yankees fail to reach the postseason.

They haven't officially clinched anything, but Baseball-Reference, FanGraphs, ESPN and PECOTA all put the Bronx Bombers at either a 99.9 or 100.0 percent chance of October baseball.

At this point, it's really just a question of seeding and what sort of momentum the Yankees can carry into the playoffs—both of which could hinge on when exactly and how emphatically Aaron Judge returns to the lineup.

Buy or Sell Each MLB Playoff Contender Advancing

As such, that will be the crux of our focus today, after a look at the current relevant standings and a couple of noteworthy injury updates.

Yankees Postseason Seed Odds, per FanDuel as of Sunday morning

As has been the case for a while now, New York is looking destined for the AL's No. 4 seed.

However, there is a gigantic four-game series still to come against the Rays (at Yankee Stadium) in two weeks. If New York manages to sweep Tampa Bay, the Yankees would effectively gain 4.5 games in the standings, as that would also flip the head-to-head tiebreaker in their favor.

Moreover, with New York having home games against the Rockies and Mets on tap for this week while the Rays have to deal with Atlanta and Houston, this AL East race could get mighty interesting in a hurry.

CF Trent Grisham is back on the IL with another hamstring strain suffered on Friday. He missed about three weeks earlier this season with a similar injury, but this one might knock him out for the rest of the year. However, he was only hitting .167/.261/.346 over his last 46 games, so cementing Spencer Jones in center while working Jasson Domínguez back into the outfield mix might not be a bad thing.

RHP Clarke Schmidt made another rehab appearance on Wednesday, just three days after his previous one. He allowed one run in two innings with three strikeouts. They clearly intend to bring him back as a middle/bulk reliever for the home stretch, and he could be a real asset in the sixth/seventh inning in the postseason.

OF Aaron Judge did pre-game work throughout this past week's road trip and is expected to face live pitching (possibly Schmidt?) at Yankee Stadium on Monday. Per MLB.com's Bryan Hoch , Judge wants to face live pitching "a couple of times, at least, before I get back in a game." But the general vibe seems to be that he should be back this week, perhaps for the series finale against the Rockies.

In the more than three months since Judge's last AB on May 31, the Yankees have had one of the most lackluster offenses in the majors.

They entered play on Sunday with a .227 batting average, a .295 on-base percentage and a .387 slugging percentage, averaging 4.07 runs per game with a FanGraphs Offense rating of minus-32.8 dating back to June 1.

29th, 30th, 26th, 25th and 29th, respectively.

In spite of that team-wide power outage, they've managed to go a respectable 45-38 behind what has arguably been the best pitching staff in the majors over the past two months.

Make no mistake about it, though: If those offensive numbers continue into October, it will be a brief stay in the postseason.

Imagine, however, that Judge comes back like nothing ever happened.

Imagine a career .291/.411/.611 hitter—MLB's top slugger since his arrival in 2016—returning to his throne, relegating Heliot Ramos (and what has been a .145/.289/.261 triple-slash with the Yankees) to a reserve role and giving this lineup the type of feared presence that it has been desperately lacking for months.

Whether the Yankees come back to win the AL East or not, don't they instantly become the clear favorite to represent the American League in the World Series if Judge resumes his Ruthian ways?

And if he does come back for a solid final 16-18 games, we're done with the "Yeah, he's great during the regular season, but he can't deliver in October" poppycock, right?

Judge hit .500/.581/.692 during New York's seven-game stay in the 2025 postseason and now has an .822 OPS and 17 home runs in 65 games played in his postseason career. He definitely hasn't been as potent during the postseason as he typically is during the regular season, but those are hardly "choke artist" numbers.

What if instead of coming back and quickly getting back to "Peak Judge" levels of greatness, he picks up right where he left off in May, matching the .550 OPS that he posted over his final 16 games before admitting defeat on the rib injury and going on the IL?

Holding down the fort until Judge comes back to the rescue has been the unspoken goal for a while now, with hopes that getting him back into the lineup would somehow be the key to Ben Rice and Cody Bellinger mashing again like they did through the first two months.

But while a .550 OPS wouldn't be drastically worse than what they've gotten collectively from his fill-ins over the past few months, finally getting Judge back without really getting Judge back could break New York's psyche.

Goodness only knows what Judge will look like when he returns, but he couldn't ask for a much more favorable landing strip than possibly starting his comeback against the Rockies, the Mets and the Twins.

The first two are last and third-to-last in the NL standings. The latter ranks fifth-worst in the majors in runs allowed per game this season, and he has a career .395/.510/.684 triple-slash in 21 games played at Target Field.

Most likely, we'll see clear signs of rust, but also some clear reminders that Judge has been the best hitter on the planet over the past five seasons; a strikeout rate of at least 30 percent, but with a .260 batting average and one home run for every 16 trips to the plate, one of which temporarily threatens to go into orbit.

If he's better than that, the No. 1 seed and a return to the World Series is very much still in play.

articles.title: Shohei Ohtani Returns to Dodgers After Missing 4 Games With Injury, Starting Lineup Revealed
articles.summary: After missing four straight games, four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani will make his return to the Los Angeles Dodgers on Monday night against the Cincinnati Reds.
articles.body:
After missing four straight games, four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani will make his return to the Los Angeles Dodgers on Monday night against the Cincinnati Reds.

Los Angeles also recalled right-handed pitcher Emmet Sheehan and optioned right-handed pitcher Bobby Miller.

Dodgers manager Dave Roberts had previously said on Sunday that "if nothing else changes," he anticipated Ohtani playing on Monday.

While Ohtani is back in the lineup, Roberts said on Sunday—per The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya —that it was "unlikely" that Ohtani would pitch again in 2026.

He further addressed the matter on Monday:

Since Ohtani is designated as a two-way player, he would've had to go on the injured list for a minimum of 15 days instead of 10.

"That'd be more of a deterrent," Roberts said Saturday of potentially placing him on the IL, per Doug Padilla of the Associated Press.

There was some progress over the weekend, though, as Padilla noted Roberts said Ohtani took swings in the batting cages Saturday after not doing so the previous two days and did not report feeling discomfort.

"I feel that it's gotten a lot better given his demeanor the last couple days," Roberts said. "What I have learned about Shohei is when he doesn't feel well, physically, he gets more short, and it's just not the same personality, which makes sense. And so I think the last couple days he's gotten a lot more loose and easygoing."

Ohtani has not pitched since July 3 as the Dodgers manage his health and has struggled of late hitting just .137 with one home run in his last 13 games. Chicago Cubs star Pete Crow-Armstrong has seized control of the National League MVP race in the meantime with Ohtani not pitching or hitting like himself.

Still, the Dodgers will surely need the six-time All-Star back and healthy if they are going to win a third straight World Series title.

While a starting rotation that features Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow gives them plenty of remaining starpower on the mound, Ohtani is an elite hitter who can carry the offense throughout October.

He launched eight home runs in 17 postseason games last year and took home the National League Championship Series MVP in the win over the Milwaukee Brewers.

Los Angeles (86-57) holds a 10-game lead in the NL West and currently holds the No. 2 seed over the Atlanta Braves.

articles.title: Shohei Ohtani returning to Dodgers' lineup vs. Reds after 4-game absence
articles.summary: Ohtani hadn't missed that many consecutive games during his two seasons with the Dodgers. However, he likely will not pitch again in 2026.
articles.body:
After sitting out for the past four games, Shohei Ohtani is back in the Los Angeles Dodgers' lineup for Monday's matchup with the Cincinnati Reds and he will bat leadoff.

Ohtani nearly batted as a pinch-hitter in Sunday's 7-5 win over the Washington Nationals. He prepared to hit in the eighth inning with the Dodgers down 5-4. Had Alex Freeland or Max Muncy reached base to begin the frame, Ohtani would have gone to bat in place of Alex Call. But Freeland popped out in foul territory and Muncy flew out to left field.

Despite Ohtani not pinch-hitting, the Dodgers took the lead when Call hit a single, Tommy Edman drew a walk and Mookie Betts hit a three-run home run to take the lead.

Ohtani being available to pinch-hit Sunday was presumably a precursor to him being in Monday's starting lineup. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts confirmed after Sunday's win that he expected Ohtani to play .

The reigning National League MVP missed the past four games while recuperating from left biceps, right knee and neck issues that took their toll, notably after striking out four times in a game last week, to the point where the Dodgers felt he would benefit from resting.

In August, Ohtani had a slash average of .241/.322/.422, far below his numbers during the previous four months of the season despite still hitting six home runs.

The question was whether or not Ohtani would recover with a longer break and go on the injured list. The Dodgers had to make a decision on that by Sunday in order to backdate an IL stint by three days , per MLB rules.

However, putting Ohtani on the IL came with some complications. Pitchers have to stay on the IL for a minimum of 15 days, unlike 10 days for position players, and that would apply to Ohtani as a two-way player. The Dodgers didn't want to be without Ohtani in the lineup for more than two weeks, especially with 19 games remaining in the regular season.

While Ohtani is still officially a two-way player in MLB's view, he appears to be done as a pitcher for the remainder of the 2026 season. The Dodgers haven't reached that decision with certainty, but the calendar and necessary timeline for Ohtani to return to the mound aren't syncing up, Roberts pointed out.

"If you're looking at the calendar, how much he's thrown in the last week, I think we can all do the math," Roberts said, via MLB.com .

Ohtani hasn't pitched since July 3, primarily due to his left knee injury. In 14 starts, he registered a 1.79 ERA and 8-2 record with 95 strikeouts in 85 2/3 innings. The Dodgers have been concerned that trying to work his way back to pitching eventually affected his performance as a hitter with the biceps and neck issues developing.

Without Ohtani, the Dodgers still have a starting rotation with Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow. Eric Lauer has filled in for Roki Sasaki, who is currently on the IL due to a blister issue . Sasaki could start when he returns, but will likely be used as a reliever during the postseason.

Additionally, Emmet Sheehan was recalled from Triple-A on Monday. In an earlier stint with the Dodgers this season. he compiled a 5.29 ERA and allowed 93 hits in 95 1/3 innings. That resulted in a demotion to Oklahoma City, where he registered a 1.50 ERA with 24 strikeouts in 18 innings.

articles.title: Yankees' Aaron Judge activated off IL after missing 3 months due to stress fracture in rib, will return vs. Rockies

The New York Yankees star will rejoin their lineup on Tuesday against the Colorado Rockies after missing the last three months with a stress fracture in his rib . The Yankees officially activated Judge on Sunday night.

Judge joined the team for its games against the Los Angeles Angels and Padres while continuing his recovery process. Boone was optimistic that an MLB return was inching closer for the Yankees captain.

"He's here to kind of continue to ramp up baseball activities," Boone said last Monday. "We're getting closer, but we feel good about where he's at."

The three-time AL MVP has been slowly ramping up his recovery going from playing catch in mid-August to taking batting practice off a pitching machine earlier this month.

articles.body: Former Major League pitcher Thomas Pannone threw a nine-inning perfect game Monday night, leading the Triple-A Nashville Sounds to a 3-0 win over the Durham Bulls. BREWERS FLAMETHROWER JACOB MISIOROWSKI SETS MLB RECORD FOR PITCHES OVER 100 MPH IN DOMINANT START Pannone put together an unblemished stat line, racking up nine shutout innings with zero hits, zero walks, and eight strikeouts. Instead, he fired consecutive strikes to battle all the way back, retiring the hitter to lock up the final out. For this left-hander, flirting with baseball history is nothing new. In fact, the Yankees opted not to give Judge a minor-league rehab assignment. Manager Aaron Boone noted there were more creative ways to build Judge’s stamina for a postseason run in September, which includes potentially playing in games with the Yankees and being pulled before nine innings are complete. Judge has been working his way back since he was cleared to do baseball activities in August. He was simply hitting off a tee, or getting soft toss, before he could take real batting practice on the field. He was seen in San Diego with the team during their West Coast road trip hitting before games. JAZZ CHISHOLM JR SAYS KNICKS CHAMPIONSHIP PARADE FUELS HIS WORLD SERIES HUNGER WITH YANKEES Judge has also been facing a high-velocity pitching machine, while doing outfield and baserunning drills to increase his stamina and get him ready for his role in right field once again. Either way, the Yankees get back their three-time MVP outfielder and a key cog in their hopes of returning to the World Series. New York is still four games behind the AL East-leading Tampa Bay Rays, but they own the top American League Wild Card slot with a nine-game lead heading into Tuesday’s start against the Rockies. At 81-62, the Yankees will be gunning for that top spot in the East, especially considering the winner of it will likely own the top AL playoff spot for the postseason. The Boston Red Sox are also right behind the Yankees at 80-65 thus far. Judge was hitting .248/.375/.533 with 17 homers and 38 RBI before hitting the injured list on June 5. The Yankees went 45-38 in the 83 games he’s missed. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP While the offense struggled to pick up the slack left by Judge, the pitching staff has been stellar throughout his absence. Thus, Judge’s return couldn’t be coming at a better time for the Yankees, as they hope to match their pitching prowess with more consistent offense during this final regular-season push.

articles.title: 4 takeaways from Braves-Phillies: Ronald Acuña Jr. looks very back, the Phillies' bullpen could be their downfall and more
articles.summary: These two familiar rivals will meet against next weekend in Atlanta.
articles.body:
The top of the National League East played itself to a stalemate this holiday weekend in Philadelphia, as the visiting Atlanta Braves and the hosting Phillies split a four-game set, two wins apiece. It was a captivating showdown between familiar rivals, one packed with impressive performances and knife's edge moments. But in the end, Walt Weiss' Braves left the Citizens Bank Park thunderdome with the same four-game division lead with which they arrived . Much happened — and little, too. At this point, the division is Atlanta's to lose.

That said, despite the dwindling of the baseball calendar, these clubs are not finished with each other yet. Three more regular-season games remain next weekend in Georgia. And, of course, there's always the opportunity for a big-time rendezvous come October.

The most consequential swing of the series — and perhaps Atlanta's entire season — came Sunday afternoon via the suddenly en fuego Ronald Acuña Jr . With the Braves down three and a pair on, the electrifying outfielder tied things up with a three-run crowd-silencer. After warding off six consecutive fastballs from Philly reliever Alex McFarlane, Acuña put the seventh, a 100.5-mph four-seamer, into the seats. As he rounded the sacks, the ever-emotive slugger unleashed his elaborate cornucopia of long-ball celebrations, much to the displeasure of the booing Philadelphia crowd.

It has been a stop-and-start year for Acuña . Twice he was pushed to the IL due to left hamstring tightness. As recently as last week, his numbers looked underwhelming at best. Fastballs, particularly those up and above the strike zone, were giving him fits. But on Wednesday against Washington, he took a heater out for just the second time this season. It was a harbinger of things to come.

In all, Acuña went 7-for-15 with two doubles and two homers against Philadelphia. His blast off a Zack Wheeler sweeper on Saturday prompted a cutting response from the veteran hurler, who tossed shade on Acuña's big-fly theatrics.

"Our guy just rounds the bases — who hits 50 here," he said, referring to MLB home run leader Kyle Schwarber.

Acuña responded to Wheeler's criticism with that dramatic long ball the following day. But a ninth-inning, one-out, full-count walk during Monday's loss was perhaps even more instructive of just how locked in Acuña is right now. He took three elevated fastballs from a dialed Jesús Luzardo before spitting on a back-foot slider to draw a huge free pass. Luzardo ultimately stranded Acuña on first , but the Phillies will be hoping the Braves' superstar cools off before the two teams meet again.

The Phillies' arms kept Atlanta's lefty bats quiet

Atlanta's typically dangerous left-handed swingers went a combined 10-for-59 with just two doubles and no homers during the four-game set. Drake Baldwin delivered a relatively powerless 5-for-18. Michael Harris II was held to two singles. Matt Olson had only one knock and one walk in 15 trips to the dish.

It's no surprise that Philadelphia's magnificent left-handed tandem of Cristopher Sánchez and Luzardo were able to keep same-sided swingers at bay. Sánchez has been brilliant all season. Luzardo owns the lowest ERA in the National League (2.01) since June 1 and delivered a masterclass complete-game shutout on Monday . Both should finish in the top five of NL Cy Young voting.

More notable, then, was that Philadelphia hurlers not named Sánchez or Luzardo limited Braves hitters to an 8-for-47 line. Baldwin was the only Atlanta lefty with multiple knocks off a righty. Saturday starter Wheeler and Sunday starter Aaron Nola each surrendered just one hit to a lefty batter. That's a massive development, considering how thin Atlanta's lineup is on righties beyond Acuña.

It's also a testament to the humming-on-all-cylinders Philadelphia starting staff. Everybody but Sánchez went through an extended lull at some point this year, but Wheeler, Nola and Luzardo have all gotten their seasons back on track. The same is true for Andrew Painter, the only Phillies starter who didn't throw in this series.

The Phillies' bullpen is walking a tightrope

In contrast to the starters, Phillies relievers allowed seven earned runs across eight innings of work in the series, a concerning trend for a unit treading water. It'd already been a difficult stretch for Orion Kerkering before the sweeper-heavy righty was touched for a pair in the eighth inning Friday. Kerkering's dip had opened the door for the rookie McFarlane, who'd been gradually climbing up skipper Don Mattingly's trust tree. Then he got popped by Acuña on Sunday.

The team's two most reliable options, Jhoan Duran and Jonathan Bowlan, both coughed up runs over the weekend as well. Mattingly's decision to let Luzardo finish his game was likely motivated, at least in part, by the team's undermanned relief corps.

Part of the blame for the bullpen shortage falls on president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski. The exec's lone deadline bullpen addition, Caleb Kilian, made just four appearances as a Philly before landing on the IL due to an oblique strain. That's bad luck. Not acquiring anyone else was bad process.

At this point, only Duran and Bowlan are 100 percent dependable. Everyone else is making you sweat. Maybe one or more of Kerkering, McFarlane, José Alvarado or Brooks Raley can ride a hot stretch and gain Mattingly's trust. But it's seeming more and more likely that this unreinforced bullpen will end up being Philadelphia's October downfall.

Atlanta's pitching is better than you think

The Phillies, by a wide margin, hold the starting pitching advantage in this matchup. If you were to construct a starting rotation from these two teams, it would be one Brave (Chris Sale) and four Phillies (Sánchez, Wheeler, Nola and Luzardo). But across four games, Atlanta proved once again that its entire staff might be superior to Philadelphia's.

Tyler Mahle and Grant Holmes, the hurlers likely to toe the slab in Games 2 and 3 behind Sale in a playoff series, were both outstanding over the weekend. They each threw six scoreless; Mahle on Sunday, Holmes on Monday. Neither have knock-you-over stuff, but Mahle and Holmes are cunning operators who know how to rack up outs.

More importantly, Atlanta's bullpen was masterful, as it's been all season. Only the Yankees and Red Sox have lower relief ERAs and WHIPs than the Braves. Dylan Lee has evolved into the perfect neutralizer for Philadelphia's lefties. The ageless Raisel Iglesias keeps on trucking. And besides one mistake to Kyle Schwarber, the 21-year-old Didier Fuentes was impressive across two multi-inning outings. Destined for a rotation spot next season, Fuentes could emerge as a secret weapon for Atlanta in the playoffs.

articles.title: Shohei Ohtani returns in Dodgers' win over Reds after 4-game absence, likely done pitching this season
articles.summary: Ohtani hadn't missed that many consecutive games during his two seasons with the Dodgers. However, he likely will not pitch again in 2026.
articles.body:
After sitting out for the past four games, Shohei Ohtani made his return to the Los Angeles Dodgers' lineup on Monday night.

Ohtani was the leadoff batter and jumped back in the lineup as their designated hitter in the Dodgers' 6-3 win over the Cincinnati Reds at Dodger Stadium. He struck out twice and was walked once in the win.

Ohtani nearly batted as a pinch-hitter in Sunday's 7-5 win over the Washington Nationals. He prepared to hit in the eighth inning with the Dodgers down 5-4. Had Alex Freeland or Max Muncy reached base to begin the frame, Ohtani would have gone to bat in place of Alex Call. But Freeland popped out in foul territory and Muncy flew out to left field.

Despite Ohtani not pinch-hitting, the Dodgers took the lead when Call hit a single, Tommy Edman drew a walk and Mookie Betts hit a three-run home run to take the lead.

Ohtani being available to pinch-hit Sunday was presumably a precursor to him being in Monday's starting lineup. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts confirmed after Sunday's win that he expected Ohtani to play .

The reigning National League MVP missed the past four games while recuperating from left biceps, right knee and neck issues that took their toll, notably after striking out four times in a game last week, to the point where the Dodgers felt he would benefit from resting.

In August, Ohtani had a slash average of .241/.322/.422, far below his numbers during the previous four months of the season despite still hitting six home runs.

The question was whether or not Ohtani would recover with a longer break and go on the injured list. The Dodgers had to make a decision on that by Sunday in order to backdate an IL stint by three days , per MLB rules.

However, putting Ohtani on the IL came with some complications. Pitchers have to stay on the IL for a minimum of 15 days, unlike 10 days for position players, and that would apply to Ohtani as a two-way player. The Dodgers didn't want to be without Ohtani in the lineup for more than two weeks, especially with 19 games remaining in the regular season.

Despite a bad night at the plate from Ohtani, the Dodgers still rolled to the three-run win thanks in part to a three-run homer from Teoscar Hernandez in the sixth inning. That put them up 5-1 at the time.

The Dodgers now sit at 87-57 on the season after the win, which was their fifth straight. They hold a double digit lead in the NL West race, too.

While Ohtani is still officially a two-way player in MLB's view, he appears to be done as a pitcher for the remainder of the 2026 season. The Dodgers haven't reached that decision with certainty, but the calendar and necessary timeline for Ohtani to return to the mound aren't syncing up, Roberts pointed out.

"If you're looking at the calendar, how much he's thrown in the last week, I think we can all do the math," Roberts said, via MLB.com .

And while he didn't rule it out completely, Ohtani confirmed after the game that pitching wasn't going to be his focus for the rest of the season.

"Most likely no," Ohtani said when asked if he was going to try to pitch again, via SportsNet LA . "I'm going to be focusing on hitting moving forward."

Ohtani hasn't pitched since July 3, primarily due to his left knee injury. In 14 starts, he registered a 1.79 ERA and 8-2 record with 95 strikeouts in 85 2/3 innings. The Dodgers have been concerned that trying to work his way back to pitching eventually affected his performance as a hitter with the biceps and neck issues developing.

Without Ohtani, the Dodgers still have a starting rotation with Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow. Eric Lauer has filled in for Roki Sasaki, who is currently on the IL due to a blister issue . Sasaki could start when he returns, but will likely be used as a reliever during the postseason.

Additionally, Emmet Sheehan was recalled from Triple-A and is starting Monday's game. In an earlier stint with the Dodgers this season. he compiled a 5.29 ERA and allowed 93 hits in 95 1/3 innings. That resulted in a demotion to Oklahoma City, where he registered a 1.50 ERA with 24 strikeouts in 18 innings.

articles.title: Aaron Judge's Return Is About More Than Just Saving Yankees Offense
articles.summary: Just so everyone remembers the stakes ahead of Aaron Judge's return, it's really weird to behold an all-time New York Yankees great who lacks a World Series ring.
articles.body:
Just so everyone remembers the stakes ahead of Aaron Judge's return, it's really weird to behold an all-time New York Yankees great who lacks a World Series ring.

The Yankees have activated Judge ahead of Tuesday's game against the Colorado Rockies. Out since May 31 with a right rib injury, he had signaled his readiness for action by taking live batting practice at Yankee Stadium on Monday. With no plans for a rehab assignment in place, his activation was the next logical step.

The Yankees don't necessarily need the three-time MVP to hit the ground running right away. It would be hard to lose a 9.0-game edge in the Wild Card standings with just 19 games left. Per Tankathon , the Yankees also have the second-easiest remaining schedule of any AL East team. Heck, they might even erase the Tampa Bay Rays' 4.0-game lead in the division.

Yankees without Judge: .536 W/L%, .681 OPS

Nine teams have won more games than the Yankees since Judge went down, and 26 have a better OPS. You don't need to strain to see the inference that they can only be an elite team if they get back the same Aaron Judge who's on track to be a first-ballot Hall of Famer.

Aaron Judge Proves Even Hall of Fame Resumes Can Be Lacking

That last part isn't controversial, is it? Surely we can all agree that Judge is on the path to Cooperstown.

The 34-year-old is one of only 13 players to win as many as three MVPs, and he has a legitimate case as the best right-handed hitter to ever live. Among righty hitters with at least 5,000 plate appearances, Judge leads all with a .611 slugging percentage and a 176 wRC+.

And yet, there is the complication of how to place Judge in the pantheon of Yankees GOATs.

According to rWAR, he's the sixth-best hitter the Yankees have ever had behind Babe Ruth , Lou Gehrig , Mickey Mantle , Joe DiMaggio and Derek Jeter . It feels like appropriate company for Judge… until you realize that those other five guys each won at least five World Series rings.

The best defense of Judge is that he plays in a different era. Before 1968, the best teams in the AL and NL went straight to the World Series. When Jeter was winning his five rings, he and the Yankees only had to survive a four-team AL playoff field between 1995 and 2011.

Judge has never known anything smaller than a five-team field. There's just so much more that can go haywire in his era. To wit, that wasn't your imagination: the Arizona Diamondbacks really were in the 2023 World Series.

Yet to absolve Judge of his ringlessness based on this argument is to miss the mark like he missed that catch in the 2024 World Series.

Bringing that up would be a cheap shot if it wasn't just so darn in theme with Judge's playoff résumé. Whereas he has a 1.022 OPS for his career in the regular season, his playoff OPS is just .822. That's a 200-point difference.

Demons? Demons. Judge will either slay them or he won't, and his legacy will or won't change accordingly.

Aaron Judge and the Yankees May Never Get a Better Shot

Even with all of that said, what if Judge is about to rejoin a Yankees team that is the favorite to represent the American League in the World Series?

In the context of the 2026 World Series race, the Yankees being the AL favorite is hardly beyond the pale. Both FanGraphs (10.1%) and FanDuel (+800) have the Yankees down as the favorite to survive the American League. It doesn't hurt that this year's AL field is not much more than a pillow fight.

Even this late in the season, two of the AL's division leaders aren't even 10 games over .500. Only four of the league's six projected playoff teams have a positive run differential, and the Yankees' (+117) is 70 runs better than that of the Rays (+47).

If this is the gateway to a "Why Not the Yankees?!" rallying cry, let's turn up the volume with these stats:

Starting Pitching: Leads MLB with a 3.34 ERA

With respect to Cam Schlittler , Max Fried and company, that last one is even more key to the Yankees' World Series chances than the first two.

The Yankees have all those homers even though they have gotten just 17 from Judge, who has four different 50-homer seasons on his record. They stand to become more powerful with him, and thus better equipped to dominate an October landscape where nothing moves the ball forward like the long ball.

The AL field feels like a throwback to 2024, when a middling 92-win Cleveland Guardians team ultimately stood between the Yankees and the World Series in the ALCS. Except this time, they may not have to worry about finding a Los Angeles Dodgers juggernaut on the other side.

The back-to-back World Series champions are 31-27 since July 1, and the only player who's been on Judge's level in recent seasons is on the fritz. Shohei Ohtani is unlikely to pitch again before 2026 is over, and he had been slumping at the plate (i.e., .703 OPS, 4 HR) for 24 games before Dave Roberts finally gave him a break from hitting duties.

Will Aaron Judge Be Up to Carrying the Yankees?

Even if the Yankees plus a healthy, productive Judge is a championship-caliber recipe on paper, there's one issue: Even if they know he's healthy, they don't know how productive he can be yet.

He's been on the sidelines for three months, and the only bright side of that is that it's not his first rodeo with a long absence in the middle of a season. He's previously had three other IL stints that lasted at least a month, and here's how the before/after looks in retrospect:

That Judge's OPS dropped off after all three of these injuries stands out, but there are asterisks on all three. The 2018 and 2019 injuries concern lopsided plate appearance comparisons. While he wasn't as good after his toe injury in 2023 as he was before, nobody ever objected to a .965 OPS.

So, let's get down to what really matters: The Yankees will know when Aaron Judge is Aaron Judge again when he starts creaming fastballs.

Between 2022 and 2025, no hitter was as dangerous against any pitch as Judge was against four-seam fastballs. We're talking a Run Value of +110, whereas the next-best for any hitter was Juan Soto's +83 against four-seamers.

This largely held true at the outset of this year… until the pain apparently became too much. After originally hurting his rib on April 26 , Judge's production really began to slip on May 7. Before then, he had an .818 SLG and 23.2 Whiff% against four-seamers. After, he slipped to a .250 SLG and a 35.1 Whiff%.

Again, the Yankees don't need Judge to save their season. The remainder of the regular season can function as a de facto ramp-up, hopefully setting him up to go full Judge in October. If he does, the history books are going to need rewrites.

If he doesn't, the road ahead will consist of an all-but-certain lockout and Judge turning 35 years old on April 26, 2027. Even on a generally old Yankees roster, that age is still going to stand out as, well, kind of ancient.

Clearly, "Wait till next year" is not something Judge or any other Yankee will want to be saying when 2026 is over.

Stats courtesy of Baseball Reference , FanGraphs and Baseball Savant .

articles.title: B/R's Undisputed MLB Shortstop Rankings
articles.summary: There is a solid case to be made that shortstop is the most important position on the diamond, and it is perennially home to some of the biggest stars in the sport as a result.
articles.body:
There is a solid case to be made that shortstop is the most important position on the diamond, and it is perennially home to some of the biggest stars in the sport as a result.

Kansas City Royals star Bobby Witt Jr. has firmly established himself as the face of the position in recent seasons, but behind him is an impressive collection of established veterans and rising stars.

Focusing solely on the 2026 season, we've ranked the shortstop performance of all 30 MLB teams.

The important distinction there is shortstop units as a whole, not individual players. That will be important in cases like the Detroit Tigers, where Kevin McGonigle has been fantastic, but has also split his time almost evenly between shortstop and third base.

Offensive and defensive contributions were both weighted heavily, and where teams are leaving the position at the end of 2026 was also a consideration. Looking at you, Kaelen Culpepper and the Minnesota Twins!

Ezequiel Tovar ranks 140th among 141 qualified hitters with a 54 OPS+ on the year, and he has also slid from a Gold Glove winner to a slightly below-average defender (-2 DRS, 0 OAA) in just two short years. Despite those struggles, he has started 119 games at shortstop, and he has four years remaining on his seven-year, $63.5 million extension.

Supporting Cast: Andruw Monasterio, Marcelo Mayer, Isiah Kiner-Falefa

It has been another injury-plagued season for Trevor Story following his 2025 rebound. When he has managed to take the field, he has posted a 71 OPS+ and a 31.7 percent strikeout rate in 48 games. After Marcelo Mayer received a brief trial, suffered an injury and was eventually traded, Andruw Monasterio provided serviceable play at shortstop in Story's absence.

Primary Starter: Taylor Walls Supporting Cast: Ben Williamson, Jorge Mateo

The Rays continue to use glove-first Taylor Walls as their primary shortstop, as he has made 109 starts at the position, despite hitting a punchless .218/.304/.292 on the year. Former top prospect Carson Williams has had three separate stints on the big league roster this year, going a combined 4-for-37 with 13 strikeouts.

Primary Starter: No One Supporting Cast: Mauricio Dubón, Ha-Seong Kim, Jim Jarvis, Jorge Mateo

The Braves signed Ha-Seong Kim to a one-year, $20 million deal during the offseason, but shortstop has been a revolving door. Utility man Mauricio Dubón leads the team with 43 starts, and the four players listed above have hit a combined .222/.275/.329 on the year. On a positive note, they do rank 13th in total defensive value at the position.

Primary Starter: J.P. Crawford Supporting Cast: Colt Emerson

With J.P. Crawford in the final season of a five-year, $51 million deal, the Mariners tried transitioning to top prospect Colt Emerson as the starting shortstop in June, with Crawford shifting to third base. However, he hit just .190/.246/.335 in 69 games while playing through a wrist injury that eventually required season-ending surgery, and now the position is in flux looking ahead to 2027.

Primary Starter: George Lombard Jr. Supporting Cast: José Caballero, Anthony Volpe

José Caballero was tasked with holding down the fort at shortstop when Anthony Volpe was sidelined to start the year, and if not for his early production, the Yankees would rank even lower. Volpe (194 PA, 82 OPS+) struggled upon returning, and touted rookie George Lombard Jr. (99 PA, 79 OPS+) has not been an upgrade since taking over as the starter.

Supporting Cast: Joey Ortiz, David Hamilton

The Brewers passed the baton from light-hitting Joey Ortiz to top prospect Cooper Pratt at shortstop on June 16, shifting Ortiz into a third base platoon with David Hamilton. All three have started games at shortstop in the past month, and the unit has produced a .228/.313/.309 line. Still, Pratt is the long-term answer after signing an eight-year, $50.75 million extension before his debut.

Supporting Cast: Alika Williams, Darell Hernaiz

Jacob Wilson will be a staple on the Athletics infield for the foreseeable future after inking a seven-year, $70 million extension in February, but a left shoulder injury sidelined him for a month in May and eventually required season-ending surgery in August. In his absence, Alika Williams (190 PA, .273/.310/.438, 1.5 WAR) has been a nice under-the-radar contributor.

Primary Starter: Konnor Griffin Supporting Cast: Jared Triolo, Jacob Gonzalez

A 91 OPS+ and 1.3 WAR over 62 games in an injury-plagued rookie campaign might seem like a flop for Konnor Griffin after he entered the year as the No. 1 prospect in baseball, but it's easy to forget he is still only 20 years old. The future is bright, even if the present falls more into the "meh" category for Pittsburgh's shortstop production.

Primary Starter: Kaelen Culpepper Supporting Cast: Brooks Lee, Ryan Kreidler, Tristan Gray

Kaelen Culpepper made his MLB debut on Aug. 7, and he has provided a middling Twins team with reason for optimism. The 23-year-old is batting .297/.350/.451 for a 124 OPS+ with eight extra-base hits and 0.7 WAR through his first 25 games in the big leagues, and with Brooks Lee making a full-time move to third base in May, he has a clear runway to be the guy at the position going forward.

Trea Turner begins a group of established veterans who occupy the next several spots in these rankings. They are underperforming, but they still provide their teams with stability. With a .239 average and 78 OPS+ in 138 games, Turner has been a shell of the player who won the NL batting title and finished fifth in NL MVP balloting a year ago, but he has started 135 of 143 games at shortstop.

With a 100 OPS+ and 21 home runs in 121 games, Willy Adames has again been a consistent source of power production, but a career-low .289 on-base percentage and poor defense (-5 DRS, -17 OAA) have severely limited his secondary contributions. Christian Koss has taken over as the starter since Adames hit the injured list on Aug. 23 with an elbow injury.

Primary Starter: Xander Bogaerts Supporting Cast: Sung-Mun Song

Xander Bogaerts has a career-low 80 OPS+ this season, hitting .218/.318/.320 with 11 home runs and 52 RBI, but he has provided some speed (20 SB) and passable defense (-6 DRS, 2 OAA) to help push him ahead of a few other veterans. Durability also remains an underrated part of his value, as he has started 132 of 143 games.

Primary Starter: Francisco Lindor Supporting Cast: Bo Bichette

A calf injury cost Francisco Lindor two months during the first half of the season, and he's never really caught fire the way he has in the past after a slow start. His 103 OPS+ and 1.2 WAR in 86 games are still passable production, while Bo Bichette made 44 starts back at his natural position filling in for him before returning to the hot corner.

Primary Starter: Andrés Giménez Supporting Cast: Ernie Clement

Andrés Giménez proved he could play a standout shortstop down the stretch last season, which helped make it easier for the Blue Jays to let Bo Bichette walk in free agency. His defensive metrics (1 DRS, 18 OAA) are terrific, but there's not much meat on the bone offensively with a .242/.288/.352 line, leaving him a 0.9-WAR player overall.

Primary Starter: Masyn Winn Supporting Cast: JJ Wetherholt, Thomas Saggese

An elite defender (8 DRS, 15 OAA) with limited offensive impact (86 OPS+, 26 XBH), Masyn Winn has settled in as a largely one-dimensional shortstop who figures to be a perennial Gold Glove contender. He is currently sidelined with a fractured thumb, and Thomas Saggese has been on fire since being recalled from Triple-A as a replacement.

Primary Starter: Colson Montgomery Supporting Cast: Luisangel Acuña

In his first full season in the big leagues, Colson Montgomery leads all shortstops with 31 home runs. He also leads the AL with 197 strikeouts, and has batted .212/.292/.437 for a 102 OPS+ despite that power production. So while his impact has been loud, it has also been largely one-dimensional.

Primary Starter: Brayan Rocchio Supporting Cast: Angel Genao

After a 1.9-WAR rookie season in 2024 propped up by his defense and a demotion back to Triple-A last year when he logged minus-0.2 WAR in 115 games, Brayan Rocchio has officially turned a corner. The 25-year-old is hitting .246/.306/.378 with 20 doubles, 13 home runs, 60 RBI, 18 steals and 2.3 WAR while continuing to provide reliable defense.

Primary Starter: Gunnar Henderson Supporting Cast: Blaze Alexander

After 6.1, 8.8 and 5.4 WAR seasons to begin his run as an everyday player in the big leagues, the 2026 campaign has been an unquestionable step backward for Gunnar Henderson. The 25-year-old still has 22 home runs and 2.4 WAR, but his .220/.304/.399 line equates to a 99 OPS+, and his batted-ball metrics are down across the board.

Primary Starter: Kevin McGonigle Supporting Cast: Javier Báez, Zach McKinstry, John Peck

There are not five players mentioned in this article having a better overall season than Kevin McGonigle. However, with 75 starts at shortstop and 60 starts at third base, the Tigers essentially get 55 percent credit for his production. The other 45 percent has been mostly Javier Báez (74 OPS+, -0.7 WAR) and recent call-up John Peck, with an occasional Zach McKinstry start, and that drags them down to the middle of the pack.

Supporting Cast: Miguel Rojas, Hyesong Kim

With a .246/.308/.423 line and 100 OPS+ on the year, Mookie Betts has not been his usual impactful self offensively, but he has still been a 2.6-WAR player thanks in large part to his glove. The defensive metrics (7 DRS, 10 OAA) are good enough that he has a chance to join Darin Erstad (1B, OF) and Plácido Polanco (2B, 3B) as the only players to win a Gold Glove at multiple positions.

Supporting Cast: Nick Allen, Carlos Correa

Now in his fifth big league season, Jeremy Peña has racked up 21.5 WAR during his time in the big leagues. A hamstring injury cost him a month during the first half, but he has still logged a 119 OPS+ with 17 home runs and 3.1 WAR in 94 games. His rapidly approaching free agency after the 2027 season will be a major story during the offseason, especially after some summer trade rumblings .

Primary Starter: Zach Neto Supporting Cast: Oswald Peraza

Speaking of summer trade rumblings, Zach Neto looks like a legitimate candidate to be dealt this winter as the Angels continue dismantling an underperforming roster. The 25-year-old is one steal away from his third straight 20/20 campaign, and he is also on track to be the Angels' team leader in WAR for the third time in a row.

Primary Starter: Geraldo Perdomo Supporting Cast: Ildemaro Vargas

After leading NL position players with 7.1 WAR and posting a 137 OPS+ in a breakout season a year ago, Geraldo Perdomo has had a less impactful follow-up campaign. However, his standout defense (7 DRS, 13 OAA) and 102 OPS+ are still enough to make him a 4.3-WAR player, and he has started 139 of 142 games for the D-backs.

While his offense has been roughly league average through his time on the North Side, Dansby Swanson has now piled up 16.6 WAR over the first four seasons of his seven-year, $177 million contract. He has a 92 OPS+ with 18 home runs and 66 RBI, and a solid case (5 DRS, 16 OAA) for his third Gold Glove.

Slick-fielding second baseman Nico Hoerner has done a stellar job filling in for Swanson since he was sidelined on Aug. 16 with an oblique strain.

Supporting Cast: Ezequiel Durán, Nicky Lopez

Durability remains the biggest concern with Corey Seager. He has a 114 OPS+ and 2.4 WAR, but he has suited up for just 84 games while navigating a nagging back issue.

In his absence, super-utility man Ezequiel Durán has made 47 starts at shortstop. The 27-year-old is enjoying the best season of his career, hitting .277/.337/.457 for a 129 OPS+ with 26 doubles, 17 home runs, 78 RBI and 4.8 WAR.

Primary Starter: CJ Abrams Supporting Cast: Nasim Nuñez

An All-Star Game starter and a solid candidate for the NL Silver Slugger this year, CJ Abrams is hitting .264/.342/.500 for a 129 OPS+ with 30 home runs, 95 RBI and 28 steals.

However, the defensive side of his game has lagged behind his bat by a considerable margin, and based on metrics (-2 DRS, -17 OAA) he might be the worst defensive shortstop in baseball. That's how good he's been offensively, for him to still be a 4.6-WAR player.

Primary Starter: Otto Lopez Supporting Cast: Javier Sanoja

There are only eight qualified players with a .300 batting average right now, and Otto Lopez is the only shortstop in the bunch. The 27-year-old is hitting .302/.339/.439 for a 120 OPS+ with 31 doubles, 10 home runs, 63 RBI, 30 steals and 5.5 WAR in 140 games.

With standout defensive metrics (9 DRS, 12 OAA) to go along with that excellent production at the plate, he has quietly put together a top-tier season across the shortstop landscape.

Primary Starter: Elly De La Cruz Supporting Cast: Matt McLain

Elly De La Cruz has had a tantalizing combination of power and speed from the moment he broke into the big leagues, but his overall game was largely unrefined, especially when it came to plate discipline and defense.

With a 133 OPS+ and a 23-homer, 24-steal performance, the power-speed production has been as expected, but the strides he has made with his on-base ability (.336 to .360 OBP) and defense (-3 to +7 OAA) have made him the NL's best shortstop.

Primary Starter: Bobby Witt Jr. Supporting Cast: Tyler Tolbert

With an AL-leading 6.4 WAR, it has been another elite season for Bobby Witt Jr. as he continues his rise as one of the game's biggest superstars.

At the plate, he has a 132 OPS+ with 30 doubles, 17 home runs and 38 steals, and those counting numbers look even better when you consider he has only played 125 games. He has also provided more overall defensive value than any shortstop, and should be a lock for his third straight Gold Glove.

The 26-year-old is simply in a tier of his own at the position right now.

articles.title: Dodgers' Shohei Ohtani Gives Pitching Update Amid Injuries Ahead of 2026 MLB Playoffs
articles.summary: Los Angeles Dodgers two-way superstar Shohei Ohtani is not expected to pitch again this season.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Dodgers two-way superstar Shohei Ohtani is not expected to pitch again this season.

Ohtani made the declaration Monday night, telling reporters he would "most likely" not pitch again in 2026, and would be "focusing on hitting moving forward."

The 32-year-old Ohtani added, "Disappointing,. But I want to make sure that when I look back this season that I used this as an experience, a learning experience, and make sure that I use that as something to improve upon for next season."

Per ESPN's Alden Gonzalez , Ohtani has been dealing with numerous injuries recently, including discomfort in his neck and right arm, left knee soreness and an issue with his right biceps, which impacted a bullpen session on Aug. 28.

Ohtani has not pitched in a game since July 3, and he had missed four games in a row before returning to the lineup Monday and going 0-for-3 as the designated hitter in L.A.'s 6-3 win over the Cincinnati Reds.

On the heels of winning the National League MVP Award in each of his first two seasons with the Dodgers, and the American League MVP Award in his final season with the Los Angeles Angels in 2023, Ohtani was enjoying his best campaign as a pitcher this season.

In 14 starts, Ohtani went 8-2 with a career-low 1.79 ERA and 0.95 WHIP this season, plus 95 strikeouts in 85.2 innings pitched.

Ohtani seemingly won't get the chance to see the season through from a pitching perspective, although he will still be able to contribute at the plate.

By normal standards, Ohtani has had another strong year as a hitter, slashing .277/.380/.522 with 30 home runs, 80 RBI, 89 runs scored and 11 stolen bases.

However, those numbers pale in comparison to what Ohtani did over his first two seasons with the Dodgers.

In 2024, Ohtani hit .310 with 54 home runs and a career-high 130 RBI and 59 steals. He followed that up last season by clubbing a career-high 55 homers to go along with a .282 average, 102 RBI and 20 stolen bases.

Ohtani is still in the thick of the NL MVP race, but it is fair to wonder if his season being cut short as a pitcher will hurt his case against Chicago Cubs outfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong, who is slashing .281/.376/.577 with 41 home runs, 97 RBI and 35 steals.

Ultimately, the Dodgers' biggest concern is winning a third consecutive World Series, and they will need Ohtani to be at his best at the plate in order to do that.

While not having Ohtani in the playoff rotation will hurt, manager Dave Roberts should have more than enough options between Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow, among others.

articles.title: Can Shohei Ohtani overcome the pain of losing his pitching return and still give Los Angeles Dodgers a season to remember?
articles.summary: MLB News: Shohei Ohtani is back with the Los Angeles Dodgers, but his return carries a different feeling than expected. After missing four games because of ling.
articles.body: Shohei Ohtani is back with the Los Angeles Dodgers, but his return carries a different feeling than expected. After missing four games because of lingering soreness, the superstar returned Monday as the designated hitter against the Cincinnati Reds. The Los Angeles Dodgers won 6-3, but the bigger story came afterward. Ohtani is now preparing to focus on hitting, with his pitching comeback unlikely to continue this season.Shohei Ohtani returns to Los Angeles Dodgers lineup as his body forces a difficult change in plansOhtani stepped back into his familiar leadoff position after taking four days away from game action. The break came as he dealt with soreness in his left knee and right biceps, issues that had made his path back to the mound much harder.His return at the plate was not spectacular. He finished 0-for-3, struck out twice and drew one walk. But for the Los Angeles Dodgers, the most important thing was seeing Ohtani back on the field and making sure he felt healthy enough to continue.“It was certainly good to get him back out there, but there was certainly nothing to kind of write home about,” Roberts said. “To take four days off, to come out of it feeling good, I think that’s a win in itself.”That reaction says a lot about where Ohtani stands right now.The Los Angeles Dodgers are no longer treating his pitching comeback as something that needs to happen at all costs. His health has become the bigger priority, especially with the regular season moving toward its final weeks.Ohtani has not pitched since July 3. He also has not thrown since a bullpen session in Detroit on Aug. 28. With so little time left in the season, trying to rebuild his pitching workload would carry obvious risks.For Ohtani, the decision is difficult because pitching has been such an important part of his return story.Still, he understands what could happen if he pushes too hard.“I’ll be focusing on hitting,” Ohtani said through a translator after the game. “I’m confident that my overall performance should be better moving forward. The thing that I was more focused on was to make sure that the pitching wouldn’t cause the worse scenario, which was for me to not be able to play at all.”That last part may be the most important.There is little value in getting Ohtani back on the mound if doing so puts his ability to play at risk. The Los Angeles Dodgers need his bat, his speed and his presence in the lineup as they prepare for the postseason.Shohei Ohtani still has time to turn his disappointment into something meaningful for Los Angeles DodgersThe setback hurts because Ohtani had already shown how effective he could be as a pitcher this season.After returning from elbow surgery, he worked his way back into a regular pitching role and produced strong numbers. In 14 starts, Ohtani went 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA, showing that his pitching ability was still very much part of his game.That makes the current situation even more frustrating.Ohtani has spent years embracing the challenge of being both a hitter and a pitcher. Watching one side of that role disappear for the rest of the season is understandably disappointing.“But I want to make sure that when I look back this season that I use this as a learning experience and use that as something to improve upon for next season,” he said.That outlook could shape the rest of his year.Instead of allowing the disappointment to take over, Ohtani can now concentrate on getting his swing back, staying healthy and helping the Los Angeles Dodgers win. His offensive numbers remain impressive, with 30 home runs and 80 RBIs, even though his recent form has not been as strong as he would like.The Los Angeles Dodgers have also given him some breathing room.Los Angeles won all four games during Ohtani’s absence, including a sweep of the Washington Nationals. The team then welcomed him back with another victory against Cincinnati.That does not mean Ohtani is no longer essential. It simply shows that the Los Angeles Dodgers have enough depth to protect their biggest star instead of rushing him into an uncomfortable situation.The postseason will bring much bigger pressure, and Ohtani could still play a major role without throwing a single pitch.For now, his path is much clearer. He needs to recover, find his rhythm at the plate and make the most of the games still ahead.His pitching comeback may have reached an unexpected pause, but Ohtani’s season does not have to end on that disappointment. articles.title: Bobby Witt Jr.’s father shaped his baseball dream: How Bobby Witt Sr. guided the Kansas City Royals star toward MLB stardom
articles.summary: MLB News: Discover how Bobby Witt Sr.'s experiences shaped his son, Bobby Witt Jr., into a Kansas City Royals MLB star, focusing on father-son mentoring and the mental game of baseball.
articles.body: Bobby Witt Jr. didn’t have to look far for someone who understood the rigours of professional baseball. His father, Bobby Witt Sr., pitched in the Major Leagues for 16 seasons and had firsthand experience with the pressures, failures and expectations that come with reaching the highest level.Witt Sr. retired from baseball after the Arizona Diamondbacks won the World Series in 2001 and was a presence through his son’s childhood. That availability allowed him to mentor Bobby Witt Jr., not just as a father but as a mentor who knew the game inside and out.How Bobby Witt Jr.’s father shaped his baseball dream?Witt Sr. taught more than the fundamentals of baseball. His most valuable lessons were on the mental side of the game, particularly learning how to handle failure and keep level-headed when things go awry.Even as an MLB star with the Kansas City Royals, Witt Jr. has continued to lean on his father’s perspective. The two have maintained a routine of talking about games, often focused on at-bats, decision-making and the mental approach rather than dwelling on physical mistakes.That difference came in handy when Witt Jr. transitioned from a highly touted prospect to an absolute big-league star. Baseball is built on failure, and Witt Sr.’s own career experience gave him a realistic view of how players can recover from bad periods of play.The elder Witt helped manage expectations, too. Success was acknowledged, but not as an excuse to become comfortable. The real message was that it was about continuous improvement, not about patting yourself on the back for a single good performance.Bobby Witt Jr. carries a remarkable baseball family legacyThe connection between the two Witts is significant even outside of their relationship. Both the father and the son were selected very high in the MLB Draft. Bobby Witt Sr. was selected third overall by the Texas Rangers in 1985, and Bobby Witt Jr. was selected second overall by the Kansas City Royals in 2019.Together, their careers formed a rare father-son baseball lineage based on elite draft status and major league expectations.Witt Sr. also gave his son a perspective that few young players hear at home. He had played professional baseball himself and could explain the difference between talent and the consistency to remain successful at the highest level.The family's ties to baseball go even deeper. Witt Jr.'s sisters married ballplayers, too, and baseball became a large part of the family's larger circle.For Witt Jr., though, his dad’s most important impact wasn’t opening the door to baseball. It was teaching him how to deal with everything that comes after entering it. articles.title: New MLB Rumors on Potential Return of Montreal Expos Amid Exploration of Expansion Cities
articles.summary: More than 20 years after moving to Washington, D.C., and becoming the Nationals, the rebirth of the Montreal Expos reportedly could be a consideration for Major League Baseball in its pursuit of expansion.
articles.body:
More than 20 years after moving to Washington, D.C., and becoming the Nationals, the rebirth of the Montreal Expos reportedly could be a consideration for Major League Baseball in its pursuit of expansion.

According to ESPN's Jeff Passan , WatchMojo CEO Ashkan Karbasfrooshan is trying to create a team of shareholders in an effort to lure an MLB team back to Montreal.

Per Passan, multiple ownership-level sources in MLB believe Montreal is "worthy of monitoring [for an expansion team] because the demographics are impossible to ignore, as is the city's baseball history."

A major hurdle standing in the way of MLB expansion has now been cleared, opening the door for the league to potentially welcome its first expansion teams since the Tampa Bay Rays and Arizona Diamondbacks in 1998.

According to Passan, the Rays getting approved for a new ballpark and the Athletics moving to Las Vegas have allowed MLB to shift its attention toward expansion with commissioner Rob Manfred saying he wants two expansion cities to be chosen by the time he retires in January 2029.

Manfred's preference is one new team on the East Coast and one on the West Coast, opening up myriad options for MLB.

Passan listed Montreal, Salt Lake City, Nashville, Raleigh, Orlando and Portland, Oregon, as cities he expects to receive the heaviest consideration for expansion teams.

Only Montreal has supported a Major League Baseball team before among those cities, as the Expos played there from 1969 to 2004.

The Expos never won or even reached a World Series, and they only made it to the playoffs once, but they are a beloved piece of sports history in Montreal, meaning there may be an appetite for big-time baseball to return to the city.

articles.title: Yankees pitcher avoids surgery, announces he is hopeful to return this season
articles.summary: The New York Yankees may be a getting a pitcher back ahead of the MLB playoffs.
articles.body:
New York Yankees reliever Fernando Cruz revealed Monday that he will attempt to delay surgery and return before the end of the regular season.

The 36-year-old was diagnosed with a partial right UCL tear and placed on the 15-day injured list in late August.

After receiving a cortisone injection, medical staff cleared him to begin a rehab protocol rather than proceed immediately with surgery.

How his arm responds to treatment and throwing over the coming days will determine whether a return before the postseason is realistic.

This season across 61 appearances, Cruz has posted a 3.13 ERA with 67 strikeouts across 54 2/3 innings. He has been one of the more reliable arms in the Yankees bullpen all year, and manager Aaron Boone will be eager to get him back if the arm cooperates. New York is in the middle of a tight American League wild card race and every available weapon in the late innings matters as the calendar winds down.

Cruz's strikeout ability is what makes him particularly valuable in high-leverage situations. His rate of over a strikeout per inning reflects a pitcher who consistently misses bats, which is exactly the profile you want in the seventh and eighth innings during a pennant race. A healthy Cruz gives Boone another legitimate option as the Yankees push toward October.

The risk of delaying surgery is real for a pitcher with a partial UCL tear, but for a 36-year-old reliever with a chance to contribute in a playoff run, it is a calculated gamble worth taking. The next week of throwing will tell the Yankees everything they need to know about whether that gamble pays off.
